output.rationale: Only one group is allowed, so all 8 templates go into a single merged engine and there are no separation choices to make. This is what the merging agent should know. Several diffs are cleanly separate: q19 changes optimizer.cpp and column_segment.cpp, q02 changes row-group/data_table storage and plan_select_node, and q16 changes the radix/aggregate hashtable. These are also the largest gains (q19 2.14x, q02 1.97x) or touch code no other diff touches, so they should merge without trouble. The overlaps that need care: (1) src/execution/perfect_aggregate_hashtable.cpp/.hpp is changed by both q01 (4 replica states per group plus a fused int64 sum/avg/count fast path) and q13 (perfect-hash aggregate and plan_aggregate changes). Their address computations and update paths have to be reconciled. (2) physical_hash_join.cpp is changed by q09, q13, q18 and q21, join_hashtable.cpp by q09 and q21, and join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp by q13, q18 and q21 (q21 also adds bloom filters). These join and filter-pushdown heuristics are where conflicts are most likely. When a compromise is needed, the merger should favour q09's (2.07x) and q13's (1.45x) behaviour over q21's (1.21x) and q18's (1.12x). (3) Cardinality and statistics changes in q09 (relation_statistics_helper) and q18 (cardinality_estimator, relation_manager) both feed join ordering and should be checked against each other. I read the summaries and the files each diff touches, not the full patches; with a single group the patch-level conflicts don't change the grouping, only how hard the merge is.
